title: Winter Fuel Payment and Your 2025/26 Self Assessment Return
excerpt: If you received a Winter Fuel Payment and your income exceeds the relevant threshold, HMRC may recover the payment through a tax charge. People already completing Self Assessment should check the treatment on the correct year's return.
metaTitle: Winter Fuel Payment and Your 2025/26 Tax Return | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check the 2025/26 Winter Fuel Payment recovery position using the payment notice, complete income and any HMRC pre-filled figures or tax-code changes.
featuredImageAlt: A pensioner checks a winter-support payment letter against annual income evidence with an adviser, warm domestic scene.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Winter Fuel Payment: If your income is over £35,000
GOV.UK — Pensioners urged to be alert to Winter Fuel Payment scams
GOV.UK — Winter Fuel Payments charge

content:
If you received a Winter Fuel Payment and your income exceeds the relevant threshold, HMRC may recover the payment through a tax charge. People already completing Self Assessment should check the treatment on the correct year's return.

Check the payment and income year

HMRC's current guidance says the payment is taken back where total income is over £35,000, subject to the applicable rules and exceptions. For a 2025/26 return, establish the relevant payment received for that period rather than copying a figure from the following winter.

Give the accountant the payment notice, amount received and complete income information. Do not assume that a pension bank deposit alone identifies the correct figure for this charge.

The recovery route depends on your circumstances

If you complete Self Assessment, HMRC says recovery is through the tax bill. Other people may have recovery through PAYE. Receiving a payment does not automatically mean that everyone must register for Self Assessment solely for this reason.

Where HMRC has pre-populated information, check it against the actual payment and circumstances. Missing or incorrect pre-filled information still needs attention before the return is approved.

Keep the charge distinct from ordinary pension income

The Winter Fuel Payment recovery is a particular charge. It should not simply be added to State Pension income or treated as a business receipt. Your wider pension, employment, savings and other taxable income help establish the overall position.

For example, a pensioner already filing because of rental income should tell the accountant about the Winter Fuel Payment as well. Filing the rental figures alone may leave the personal return incomplete.

Be alert to payment-related scams

Use GOV.UK or your usual HMRC account route to check requests. Do not provide bank details through an unexpected message claiming that a special link is needed to retain or repay the payment.

TaxSimba can check the return information within the agreed service. Supply the payment details and any HMRC correspondence early so the accountant can identify the correct year and recovery route without guessing from the amount of your regular pension.

Put it into practice

Keep the recovery charge separate from pension income

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A pensioner already files because of rental income and also received a Winter Fuel Payment. She supplies the payment notice and complete pension, interest and rental information. The accountant checks the applicable recovery rule and any pre-filled amount for the correct year. She does not add the payment to her regular State Pension figure or assume a PAYE-code change has already settled the charge. Any duplicated collection or incorrect notice is queried using the actual account evidence.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Which payment and tax year are involved?Use the notice and amount received rather than the following winter's figure.
Is the full relevant income picture available?Gather pensions, employment, savings and other income for the threshold check.
How is HMRC recovering any charge?Reconcile Self Assessment or PAYE information and check pre-filled figures.

Two more questions you may have

Does everyone receiving a payment need a tax return?

No. Recovery routes depend on circumstances. Check the actual filing requirement rather than registering solely from a general headline.

Should the payment be added to State Pension income?

Keep the payment and any recovery charge distinct so the appropriate treatment can be checked.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Collect the payment notice and amount.
  • Identify the relevant winter and tax year.
  • Gather complete income records.
  • Compare HMRC pre-filled and coding information.
  • Resolve any duplicate or incorrect recovery entry.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Self Assessment Refund Pending: What to Check Before Chasing HMRC
excerpt: A credit in your Self Assessment account does not always mean a repayment has already been issued. Check whether a refund was requested, whether HMRC is checking it and whether any amount has been used against another liability.
metaTitle: Self Assessment Refund Pending: What to Check | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Refund pending? Reconcile the tax calculation with your HMRC account, check whether repayment was requested and retain references before following up.
featuredImageAlt: A taxpayer checks a refund request and HMRC account messages with adviser, careful bank-details confirmation no numbers.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Self Assessment tax returns: Claiming a tax refund
GOV.UK — Check when you can expect a reply from HMRC

content:
A credit in your Self Assessment account does not always mean a repayment has already been issued. Check whether a refund was requested, whether HMRC is checking it and whether any amount has been used against another liability.

Start with the return and account balance

Compare the submitted tax calculation with the statement of account. Payments on account, earlier payments, adjustments and outstanding charges can affect the amount available for repayment. The refund expected from one year's calculation may differ from the final account credit.

If the return includes CIS deductions or other tax credits, make sure the supporting figures and statements are correct. A refund should follow an accurate return, not a target amount someone has promised before reviewing the evidence.

Understand a pending status

HMRC says a repayment may show as pending in the online account. Security or other checks can delay issue. Use HMRC's current guidance and reply-time checker rather than relying on a fixed payment date quoted in an advert or online discussion.

Check bank details carefully and follow genuine requests for further information. Do not send the same repayment request repeatedly simply because the first has not completed; first establish what is happening to it.

Keep the relevant references

Retain the filing confirmation, date of the repayment request, bank details supplied, HMRC correspondence and details of any identity checks. If an accountant is helping, tell them about contact you have already had with HMRC so enquiries are coordinated.

For example, a repayment reduced by an outstanding payment on account may be an account-allocation issue rather than an error in the tax return. Amending a correct return will not necessarily solve that problem.

Know who controls the payment

An accountant can explain the calculation and assist with an agreed enquiry, but HMRC controls the checks and release of a repayment. TaxSimba should not be understood to guarantee HMRC's processing time.

Ask whether repayment follow-up work is included in your engagement. Keep any separate fee clear, and use official channels if an unexpected message asks you to pay money or disclose card details to unlock a tax refund.

Put it into practice

A calculation credit is not always the cash repayment

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A return suggests a £900 repayment, but the HMRC account shows other dated charges and payments. The taxpayer compares the calculation with the statement, checks whether a repayment request was made and records its date. He verifies bank details through the normal secure route and reads any information request. He does not amend an accurate return simply to make a pending status disappear or submit repeated requests without understanding the first one's position.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Does the statement reconcile to the calculation?Identify payments, credits and other liabilities affecting the available repayment.
Was a repayment requested and checked?Record the request date, status and any HMRC follow-up.
Is follow-up due under current guidance?Use HMRC's current reply-time route and coordinate any agent enquiry.

Two more questions you may have

Can an accountant guarantee the payment date?

No. HMRC controls processing and release. Keep the evidence and respond to genuine requests promptly.

Does a pending status prove the return is wrong?

No. It can concern processing or checks. Establish the cause before changing supported figures.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Save the submitted calculation and filing reference.
  • Download the current account statement.
  • Record the repayment request date and status.
  • Check bank details securely and retain correspondence.
  • Coordinate one evidence-based follow-up when appropriate.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Gift Aid on Self Assessment: Claim the Right Relief Without Double Counting
excerpt: Gift Aid can affect your personal tax calculation as well as the amount a charity receives. Keep an accurate record of eligible donations and distinguish them from Payroll Giving, business sponsorship and ordinary purchases.
metaTitle: Gift Aid on Self Assessment: Avoid Double Relief | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare Gift Aid donation dates and cash amounts, distinguish gross figures and Payroll Giving, and check the tax-paid condition and any carry-back timing.
featuredImageAlt: A donor reconciles charitable donation receipts and Gift Aid declarations with an accountant.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Tax relief when you donate to a charity: Gift Aid
GOV.UK — Help with charitable giving on your Self Assessment tax return

content:
Gift Aid can affect your personal tax calculation as well as the amount a charity receives. Keep an accurate record of eligible donations and distinguish them from Payroll Giving, business sponsorship and ordinary purchases.

Start with the donation actually made

Under Gift Aid, the charity can reclaim basic-rate tax on an eligible donation. A £100 qualifying donation is generally treated as £125 gross. People entitled to higher or additional-rate relief may claim the further difference through the appropriate route.

Give your accountant the actual amount paid and explain whether a statement already shows a grossed-up figure. Entering an amount already grossed up as if it were the cash donation can overstate the claim.

Check that enough tax has been paid

You must have paid enough UK Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax to cover the Gift Aid reclaimed on your donations for the year. If not, you can be responsible for the difference. A signed declaration does not remove that condition.

This can matter where income falls, allowances eliminate tax or someone makes a large donation in a year with little taxable income. Review the position rather than assuming every charity payment qualifies automatically.

Separate other giving arrangements

Payroll Giving already receives relief through payroll and should not be claimed again as an ordinary Gift Aid donation. Memberships, purchases and donations with benefits can have conditions. Shares or land given to charity involve different relief rules from cash Gift Aid.

For example, a fundraising statement showing a payment total should be checked against the charity's eligible Gift Aid amount, especially where tickets or goods were supplied.

Check timing before submitting

There are specific rules for treating certain current-year donations as made in the previous year. Any such claim needs checking before the original return is submitted; it should not be assumed available through a later amendment.

Supply TaxSimba with donation dates, amounts, charity statements and details of any other giving route. The accountant can review the claim alongside your other income and reliefs, so the same donation is neither omitted nor counted twice.

Put it into practice

Cash paid and gross donation are two views of one gift

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A charity statement shows £80 paid and £20 Gift Aid reclaimed, giving £100 gross. The donor sends both labels to the accountant rather than entering £100 as another cash payment. Payroll Giving is kept separate so relief is not claimed twice. She also checks whether enough UK Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax was paid to cover the charity's reclaim and flags any proposed prior-year treatment before the original return is submitted.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Cash amount or already grossed-up figure?Keep the statement labels clear to avoid grossing up twice.
Was enough qualifying UK tax paid?Check the condition across the year's eligible donations.
Is another giving method or carry-back involved?Separate Payroll Giving and check the specific timing and claim rules.

Two more questions you may have

Can Payroll Giving be claimed again as ordinary Gift Aid?

No. It has a different relief route. Provide the payroll evidence and avoid a duplicate claim.

Does signing a declaration remove the tax-paid requirement?

No. The donor can be responsible for a shortfall if insufficient qualifying UK tax was paid.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • List eligible charities, donation dates and cash amounts.
  • Identify any statement already showing gross figures.
  • Separate Payroll Giving and other donation types.
  • Check sufficient UK tax for Gift Aid reclaims.
  • Raise any carry-back request before original filing.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: State Pension on Self Assessment: Why Bank Payments May Not Be the Right Figure
excerpt: State Pension is generally taxable, although it is normally paid without tax deducted. If you complete Self Assessment, use the correct tax-year figure rather than assuming the total deposited in your bank is always the amount to report.
metaTitle: State Pension on Self Assessment: Use the Right Figure | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare the correct State Pension tax-year entitlement, start dates and uprating notices, and separate workplace pension income and PAYE deductions.
featuredImageAlt: A pensioner compares entitlement letter with bank deposits across tax-year boundaries, calendar and retirement folder.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Tax when you get a pension: Overview
GOV.UK — Tax when you get a pension: How your tax is paid
GOV.UK — How your State Pension is taxed

content:
State Pension is generally taxable, although it is normally paid without tax deducted. If you complete Self Assessment, use the correct tax-year figure rather than assuming the total deposited in your bank is always the amount to report.

Entitlement and payment dates can differ

HMRC explains that taxable State Pension is based on the amount you were entitled to receive over the tax year. Four-weekly bank payments and the annual uprating can make a simple bank-total calculation different from the relevant entitlement figure.

The first year of receiving State Pension may also cover only part of the tax year. Give your accountant the award notice, start date and relevant uprating information. Explain any deferred pension or lump sum because it may require separate treatment.

Other pensions need their own records

Private and workplace pensions can have PAYE deducted. Provide P60s or equivalent statements showing the gross income and tax withheld. Do not combine those payments with State Pension and enter only the total reaching your bank.

For example, a workplace pension provider may collect tax through its code partly because you also receive State Pension. The return still needs the separate income figures and the tax actually deducted through PAYE.

State Pension does not automatically require a return

Whether you need Self Assessment depends on your overall circumstances. HMRC can collect tax through other routes, including tax codes or Simple Assessment. Check the requirement rather than purchasing a return solely because you started receiving a pension.

If you already file for rental or other income, include the pension information in that return. Pension income being shown in HMRC's records does not remove the need to check the figures before approval.

Review notices alongside the return

Keep tax coding notices and any Simple Assessment correspondence so amounts are not inadvertently paid or reported twice. Changes in employment, pension providers or residence should also be explained.

TaxSimba can confirm the appropriate service and documents after reviewing your circumstances. An accurate year-by-year pension record helps the accountant reconcile the calculation with what HMRC is already collecting.

Put it into practice

Four-weekly deposits can obscure the tax-year amount

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A taxpayer starts State Pension partway through the year and receives four-weekly deposits. She provides the award notice, start date and uprating information so the relevant tax-year entitlement can be checked. Her workplace pension has PAYE deducted and is documented separately with its P60. She does not combine the net bank deposits from both pensions into one income number. Tax coding and any Simple Assessment notice are retained to help reconcile what HMRC is already collecting.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
What entitlement relates to this tax year?Use award and uprating evidence, especially in the first pension year.
Which pensions have PAYE deductions?Keep State Pension and private or workplace pension records separate.
Has HMRC used another collection route?Check coding or Simple Assessment notices alongside the return.

Two more questions you may have

Does State Pension always require Self Assessment?

No. The overall circumstances and HMRC's collection route matter. Check the filing requirement.

Is the bank total always the taxable figure?

Not necessarily. Entitlement timing and four-weekly payment dates can differ from a simple deposit total.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Collect the State Pension award notice.
  • Record start date and uprating details.
  • Gather private and workplace pension P60s.
  • Keep PAYE tax and net payments distinct.
  • Compare coding and assessment notices with the return.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: No Longer Need Self Assessment? Ask HMRC Before You Stop Filing
excerpt: You should not keep paying for unnecessary returns, but you should not ignore an HMRC notice to file either. If your circumstances have changed, check the requirement for the particular year and ask HMRC to confirm any withdrawal.
metaTitle: Leave Self Assessment: Get HMRC Confirmation First | TaxSimba
metaDescription: No longer need a return? Review all income, identify the tax year and ask HMRC to withdraw the requirement while checking final and earlier liabilities.
featuredImageAlt: A former sole trader asks an accountant to confirm an official stop-filing response rather than discarding a notice.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Self Assessment tax returns: If you no longer need to send a tax return
GOV.UK — Check if you need to send a Self Assessment tax return

content:
You should not keep paying for unnecessary returns, but you should not ignore an HMRC notice to file either. If your circumstances have changed, check the requirement for the particular year and ask HMRC to confirm any withdrawal.

Identify what changed

You may have stopped self-employment, sold a rental property or no longer have the income that originally required a return. Other reportable income or gains can still mean Self Assessment is needed, so review the whole position rather than one source in isolation.

For example, selling your last rental property might remove future rental income, but the sale and final rental year can still have reporting obligations. Closing the letting activity does not automatically close those tax years.

Ask for the correct year to be removed

HMRC allows you to say that a return is no longer needed, including for a specific tax year. Keep the request and confirmation. Stopping a subscription with an accountant or deleting an online account does not withdraw an HMRC filing notice.

If a deadline is approaching and the request has not been resolved, contact HMRC or your accountant promptly about the next step. Do not assume silence means permission to leave an issued return unfiled.

Deal with existing liabilities separately

Withdrawal of a future filing requirement does not necessarily cancel tax, interest or penalties for earlier years. Check the statement of account, payments on account and any outstanding notices.

If income has fallen, payments on account may need a separate review. Reducing them does not itself remove you from Self Assessment and can create interest if reduced too far.

Keep the decision evidence

Record the reason no return is required, the relevant income figures and HMRC's response. Review the position again if new self-employed income, rent, gains or other circumstances arise.

TaxSimba can help establish the service actually needed and identify any final-year work within the agreed scope. A responsible review may conclude that you need a final return, a different HMRC route or no further annual return after confirmation. The right outcome depends on your facts, not on automatically renewing the same service every year.

Put it into practice

Selling the last rental property can still leave final work

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A landlord sells her last rental and expects no future rental income. She still supplies final rent, sale details and any outstanding tax records for the relevant year. She checks whether gains or another income source require a return, then asks HMRC about the specific later-year filing requirement. She retains the response rather than assuming cancellation of an accountant's subscription removes the notice to file. Earlier tax, interest and penalties are checked separately.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
What changed and when?Record the end of the activity and any final income or disposal.
Does another filing reason remain?Review the whole personal position and the specific tax year.
Has HMRC withdrawn the requirement?Keep the confirmation and deal with approaching deadlines while a request is unresolved.

Two more questions you may have

Does leaving cancel old balances or penalties?

Not automatically. Resolve earlier liabilities and notices separately from future filing requirements.

Will reducing payments on account remove Self Assessment?

No. That changes advance-payment estimates, not the return requirement itself.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Describe the changed circumstances and dates.
  • List final income, disposals and other sources.
  • Identify the specific year to be withdrawn.
  • Submit the correct request and retain confirmation.
  • Check earlier balances and future changes in circumstances.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: P800 or Simple Assessment PA302: Do You Also Need a Tax Return?
excerpt: A P800 tax calculation or PA302 Simple Assessment is not the same as a Self Assessment return. Check what HMRC has sent, the tax year concerned and whether you already file before deciding what to do next.
metaTitle: P800 or Simple Assessment PA302: Check Before Paying | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Understand a P800 or PA302, compare the tax year and figures with your records and check for overlap with Self Assessment or an earlier assessment.
featuredImageAlt: A taxpayer compares two different tax-office calculation letters and a return notice with adviser.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Tax overpayments and underpayments: If you’ve not paid the right amount of tax
GOV.UK — Pay your Simple Assessment tax bill: Overview
GOV.UK — Issue 148 of agent update

content:
A P800 tax calculation or PA302 Simple Assessment is not the same as a Self Assessment return. Check what HMRC has sent, the tax year concerned and whether you already file before deciding what to do next.

Why a letter may arrive now

HMRC's October 2026 agent update says tax calculations and Simple Assessments are being issued for tax owed on bank and building society interest earned in 2025/26. Some people may receive a second assessment after HMRC receives additional interest information.

That makes it important to check the figures rather than assume a new letter always represents a completely separate debt. Keep the earlier notice and evidence of any payment alongside the latest one.

Understand the document

A P800 explains an underpayment or overpayment under HMRC's reconciliation process. A Simple Assessment tells you about a liability HMRC has calculated without requiring an ordinary Self Assessment return for that calculation.

Neither document means every recipient must buy a tax-return service. Equally, a notice based on information HMRC holds may not capture every income source or reporting obligation you have.

Check for duplication

Compare employment, pensions, interest and tax deductions with your own statements. If a second Simple Assessment includes an amount already assessed and paid, check how the payment affects the remaining balance before paying again.

If you are already registered for Self Assessment for the same year, tell HMRC or your accountant. HMRC's current guidance addresses withdrawal of a Simple Assessment where Self Assessment applies; do not simply report or pay the same liability twice.

Raise errors promptly

HMRC says queries about an incorrect Simple Assessment should be raised within 60 days of the letter. Follow the notice for payment and challenge instructions rather than treating that period as a general extension to every deadline.

TaxSimba can review an enquiry and confirm whether a return or separately agreed assistance is appropriate. Send the complete notices and your supporting figures so the accountant can identify what HMRC has calculated and what, if anything, remains outside it.

Put it into practice

A second notice needs a reconciliation, not a second guess

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A taxpayer receives a revised assessment after additional savings-interest information reaches HMRC. She keeps the earlier notice and payment evidence, then compares the year, income totals and remaining balance. If she already files Self Assessment for that year, she tells HMRC or the accountant rather than paying and reporting the same liability twice. She records the notice's query and payment instructions. A letter does not automatically mean she needs to buy an annual return service.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
What document and year is this?Distinguish a P800 calculation, Simple Assessment and a Self Assessment notice.
Does it replace or overlap earlier figures?Compare notices and payments so the same amount is not paid twice.
Are the income or tax figures wrong?Raise the issue through the specified route and within the relevant notice deadline.

Two more questions you may have

Does a PA302 mean I must file a tax return?

Not by itself. Check whether other income or an existing Self Assessment requirement creates a separate duty.

Can I ignore a Simple Assessment because I file Self Assessment?

No. Tell HMRC about the overlap and follow the appropriate correction or withdrawal process.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Keep the complete notice and issue date.
  • Identify tax year and document type.
  • Compare source income and tax-deduction statements.
  • List earlier notices and payments.
  • Record query, payment and overlap-resolution instructions.

title: Business Loans on Self Assessment: Interest, Borrowing and Repayments
excerpt: A business loan affects cash flow differently from taxable profit. The money borrowed, the repayment of that borrowing and the interest charged should not all be entered as ordinary sales or expenses.
metaTitle: Business Loans on Self Assessment: Capital vs Interest | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Separate business borrowing, loan repayments and interest, retain the use-of-funds evidence and avoid claiming the same equipment cost more than once.
featuredImageAlt: A business owner separates a loan agreement's principal balance from interest entries in ledger, calculator.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Legal and financial costs
GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Overview

content:
A business loan affects cash flow differently from taxable profit. The money borrowed, the repayment of that borrowing and the interest charged should not all be entered as ordinary sales or expenses.

Borrowing is not normally trading income

A genuine loan brings an obligation to repay. Receiving the borrowed capital is not usually a customer sale, and repaying the capital is not usually a deductible business running cost. The purchase funded by the loan needs its own tax treatment.

For example, borrowing £5,000 to buy equipment does not normally create £5,000 of sales. A later repayment does not automatically create another equipment deduction. Keep the loan and the asset purchase separately identifiable.

Interest and charges need a purpose check

Interest on qualifying business borrowing and certain finance charges can be allowable, subject to the relevant rules. Personal use or mixed use can restrict the claim. The label on the bank account does not establish how the borrowed money was actually used.

Supply the agreement, interest schedule and evidence of where the funds went. Where a payment contains both capital and interest, the accountant needs the breakdown rather than treating the whole instalment as an expense.

Different finance arrangements can differ

Hire purchase, leasing, credit cards and ordinary loans can require different analysis. Residential landlord finance costs also have separate restrictions, so do not transfer sole trader loan treatment directly to a buy-to-let mortgage.

If a lender writes off debt or the business closes before repayment, raise it with the accountant. Those events can create questions beyond the ordinary annual interest entry.

Reconcile the bank and accounts

Explain transfers from personal savings and repayments to yourself as well as bank borrowing. Owner's funds are not automatically sales, and money withdrawn for living costs is not a business expense.

TaxSimba can review finance entries within your agreed bookkeeping or tax-return service. Providing a clear capital-and-interest schedule helps the accountant avoid both overstating expenses and overlooking genuine costs, while keeping the balance owed to the lender distinct from the tax due to HMRC.

Put it into practice

A loan repayment is not another equipment purchase

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A trader borrows £4,000 and buys equipment. A later £220 instalment includes £180 loan capital and £40 interest. He keeps the loan and equipment records separately, explaining how the money was used. The £4,000 borrowing is not treated as a customer sale, and the £180 repayment is not another expense for buying the equipment. The asset's relief and any allowable business interest are checked under their own rules, including private use and financing terms.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
What did the borrowed funds finance?Provide the agreement and evidence of business or mixed use.
How does each instalment split?Separate repayment of capital from interest and relevant charges.
Has the purchase already received relief?Reconcile the asset and finance records to prevent duplicate deductions.

Two more questions you may have

Does a loan paid into the business account count as sales?

A genuine repayable loan is not ordinarily a customer receipt. Label the funding clearly.

Are hire purchase and ordinary loans always treated alike?

No. Supply the actual agreement so the arrangement and asset treatment can be checked.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Collect loan and finance agreements.
  • Trace the use of borrowed funds.
  • Obtain capital-and-interest schedules.
  • Link financed purchases to asset records.
  • Identify private use, write-offs or business closure.

title: Basis Period Transition Profits: What Still Goes on a 2025/26 Return?
excerpt: Some sole traders and partners still have transition profits to include in their 2025/26 tax calculation following basis period reform. These are separate from the ordinary profit calculation for the current tax year.
metaTitle: Basis Period Transition Profit: Check Your 2025/26 Return | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare transition-profit schedules for 2025/26, reconcile amounts already taxed and identify elections or cessation before applying any remaining spread.
featuredImageAlt: A trader reviews older transition-profit workings and remaining-year records with accountant, timeline and folders.

sources.label: GOV.UK — HS222 How to calculate your taxable profits (2026)
GOV.UK — Work out your Basis Period Reform transition profit

content:
Some sole traders and partners still have transition profits to include in their 2025/26 tax calculation following basis period reform. These are separate from the ordinary profit calculation for the current tax year.

Why earlier profits can still matter

The 2023/24 transition rules moved affected businesses towards reporting profits on a tax-year basis. Where additional transition profits arose after relevant overlap relief, spreading could apply over five years ending in 2027/28.

A business with a non-tax-year accounting date is more likely to need this checked. Not every sole trader has transition profits, and changing accountant does not create a new spreading period.

Recover the earlier calculation

Provide the 2023/24 computation, overlap relief used, 2024/25 return and a schedule of transition profit already taxed. Any election to bring amounts into charge earlier needs to be reflected in the remaining balance.

For example, an accountant cannot reliably calculate the 2025/26 allocation from the latest bank statements alone. They need to know the original transition figure and what happened in the earlier returns.

Avoid applying the same percentage blindly

The default spreading approach does not mean the same amount is always included regardless of earlier elections or cessation. HMRC's 2025/26 helpsheet explains when spreading still applies and when amounts have already been fully taxed.

If the business has ceased, remaining transition profits can need different treatment. Tell the accountant about closures, incorporation or other significant changes before the return is finalised.

Keep the current profit calculation separate

Transition profit is not new cash earned in 2025/26. It can nevertheless affect the tax calculation alongside current profits and other income. That is one reason a bill may differ from a simple percentage of this year's bank surplus.

Ask TaxSimba to confirm whether reconstructing an incomplete transition calculation is included or requires additional work. A proper handover from the previous accountant can save time. Keep the final schedule with your tax records so the remaining amount can be checked consistently in later years.

Put it into practice

Bring the original schedule, not just current bank records

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A trader with a non-tax-year accounting date changed accountants after the transition year. For 2025/26, she obtains the 2023/24 computation, overlap-relief evidence, subsequent return and schedule showing transition profit already charged. The new accountant checks remaining amounts and any earlier election before calculating the current allocation. If the trade has ceased, that is flagged separately. Transition profit is not fresh cash received this year, so a bank export alone cannot reconstruct it reliably.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
What was the original transition-profit figure?Recover the transition computation and overlap-relief evidence.
What has already been taxed or elected?Reconcile subsequent returns and any accelerated-charge election.
Has the business ceased or changed?Check whether the remaining spread needs different treatment.

Two more questions you may have

Does every sole trader have transition profit?

No. It depends on accounting dates and the transition calculation. Check the prior computation.

Can I start a new five-year spread with a new accountant?

No. The existing history follows the taxpayer. Provide the handover schedule and prior returns.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Locate the 2023/24 transition computation.
  • Collect overlap-relief evidence.
  • List transition amounts already taxed.
  • Retain elections and subsequent returns.
  • Explain cessation or major business changes.

title: Can You Claim Business Costs Paid Before You Started Trading?
excerpt: Some business costs paid before a trade begins can qualify for tax relief. The fact that a payment predates your first customer does not automatically exclude it, but the normal business-expense conditions still matter.
metaTitle: Pre-Trading Startup Expenses: Dates and Evidence | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare qualifying startup costs with dates, business purpose and commencement evidence, while separating equipment, private costs and previous relief.
featuredImageAlt: A new business founder organises genuine pre-opening expense invoices against launch-date planner.

sources.label: GOV.UK — BIM46351 - Specific deductions: pre-trading expenditure: scope - HMRC internal manual
GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Office, property and equipment

content:
Some business costs paid before a trade begins can qualify for tax relief. The fact that a payment predates your first customer does not automatically exclude it, but the normal business-expense conditions still matter.

Identify when the trade actually started

Preparing to trade and carrying on a trade are not always the same thing. Tell the accountant what you were doing, when you became ready to supply customers and when the first work or sale occurred. An HMRC registration date alone may not settle the trading start date.

Keep a timeline of preparatory activity, contracts and launch spending. This helps distinguish pre-trading costs from costs of an existing activity or a business that never began.

The seven-year rule has conditions

HMRC's pre-trading expenditure rules can cover qualifying revenue expenses incurred within seven years before commencement where they would have been deductible if incurred after the trade began. The rules do not make every historic purchase allowable.

Capital expenditure, private spending and amounts already relieved need separate consideration. Costs paid in advance for a later period should also be checked so the same expense is not deducted twice under different provisions.

A practical example

Advertising prepared for the launch of a genuine trade may need considering differently from buying an asset or paying for general personal development. Keep the invoice and explain exactly how the cost relates to the trade that commenced.

Training that creates a new skill or new activity can require a different analysis from updating existing business skills. Do not rely on a broad statement that every start-up course is deductible.

Prepare a start-up schedule

List the date, supplier, amount, purpose, private-use element and whether any reimbursement or earlier claim was made. Keep equipment purchases separate from routine costs so the accountant can apply the appropriate rules.

TaxSimba can review qualifying start-up costs within the agreed return service. Supply the evidence even if it falls before the tax year being filed, and let the accountant establish the correct treatment rather than entering every payment as an ordinary expense on the day the business launches.

Put it into practice

Before the first sale is not the same as automatically allowable

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A designer pays for launch advertising before starting a genuine trade. She keeps the invoice and a timeline showing preparation, readiness to serve clients and the first work. She separately lists a laptop and a training course, since capital items and new skills need their own treatment. The accountant checks whether the revenue cost meets the pre-trading conditions, including timing, business purpose and no earlier relief. Registration date alone does not establish every commencement fact.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
When did the trade actually commence?Provide a factual timeline, contracts and first-transaction evidence.
Would the cost qualify after commencement?Check the normal business-expense conditions and relevant pre-trading timing.
Is it capital, private or already relieved?Separate those items and avoid claiming the same amount under two routes.

Two more questions you may have

Does the seven-year rule make every old purchase deductible?

No. The expense must meet the relevant conditions. Keep the purpose, timing and prior-use history.

Are all startup courses deductible?

Not automatically. Explain what skills the course provides and its connection with the actual trade.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Build a commencement timeline.
  • List pre-trading dates, suppliers and costs.
  • Explain the business purpose of each item.
  • Separate equipment, training and private-use items.
  • Identify reimbursements or previous relief.

title: Tools, Laptops and Equipment: Expenses or Capital Allowances?
excerpt: Business equipment can qualify for tax relief, but the route depends on the item, your accounting method and how it is used. Buying through a business bank account does not automatically make the full cost deductible.
metaTitle: Tools and Laptops: Expenses or Capital Allowances? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check equipment relief using the accounting method, asset type, business use and finance details, and retain records of later disposals and replacements.
featuredImageAlt: A craftsperson reviews laptop and tools purchases with an accountant beside asset invoices and business-use notes.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Office, property and equipment
GOV.UK — Claim capital allowances: Overview
GOV.UK — Cash basis: Overview

content:
Business equipment can qualify for tax relief, but the route depends on the item, your accounting method and how it is used. Buying through a business bank account does not automatically make the full cost deductible.

Identify what was purchased

Tools, computers and machinery may be treated differently from consumables, buildings or vehicles. Keep the invoice, purchase date, payment details and an explanation of the item's role in the business.

The amount paid is not always the amount eligible for relief. Personal use, financing arrangements and particular asset rules can change the calculation.

Cash basis and traditional accounting differ

Under cash basis, many qualifying equipment purchases can be dealt with as expenses, although exceptions apply, including particular rules for cars. Traditional accounting can require capital allowances rather than an ordinary deduction for the asset's cost.

Depreciation shown in accounts is not automatically the tax deduction. The accountant may need to add it back and calculate the appropriate capital allowance separately.

Business use needs evidence

For example, a laptop used partly for private purposes should not automatically receive a 100% business deduction. Explain how it is used and retain a reasonable basis for any business proportion. Do not choose an arbitrary percentage because another trader used it.

If equipment was owned privately before entering the business, or purchased before trading began, flag that history. Its tax treatment may differ from a new asset bought solely for business after commencement.

Keep sales and replacements linked

Selling, trading in or ceasing to use an asset can affect the tax position. Provide details of proceeds and previous claims. Claiming for a replacement does not mean the earlier item's disposal can be ignored.

Where finance is involved, supply the agreement so the asset purchase, loan capital and interest are not all claimed as separate versions of the same cost.

TaxSimba can establish the appropriate treatment within the agreed service after reviewing the method and evidence. Ask before making a purchase solely for tax reasons: relief can reduce a liability, but it does not turn an unnecessary item into free equipment.

Put it into practice

An asset invoice and finance payment are not two costs

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A consultant buys a laptop used for both business and private activities and finances the purchase. She supplies the invoice, payment and finance agreement, prior accounting method and a supported use explanation. The accountant checks whether the qualifying cost is treated as a cash-basis expense or through another appropriate relief route. Interest and capital repayment remain identifiable. When the laptop is sold later, she retains the proceeds and previous claim rather than ignoring the disposal after buying a replacement.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
What item and accounting method apply?Identify asset type and cash-basis or traditional treatment before entering a deduction.
How much relates to the business?Document actual use and any private element.
Is there finance, prior ownership or a disposal?Provide the full history so costs and proceeds are handled once under the correct rules.

Two more questions you may have

Is depreciation always the tax deduction?

No. Under traditional accounting, tax adjustments and capital allowances may replace the accounts depreciation figure.

Does tax relief make an unnecessary purchase free?

No. Relief can reduce a liability but does not reimburse the whole cost. Buy for a business need and check treatment separately.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Collect invoices and acquisition dates.
  • Confirm the accounting method.
  • Describe business and private use.
  • Provide finance and previous-ownership details.
  • Track disposals, trade-ins and earlier claims.
